provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Marks one event following immediately on another, in the plainest terms available (電気を消すとすぐに子どもは寝てしまった). Unlike the literary siblings や否や and が早いか it is ordinary in speech and writing and covers habits as well as one-off past events (朝起きるとすぐに). Because it builds on the conditional と, the main clause only reports what happens: no commands, requests or intentions (帰ったらすぐに電話してください, not 帰るとすぐに).

examples.ruby: 電気[でんき]を消[け]すとすぐに子[こ]どもは寝[ね]てしまった。
examples.english: The kids fell asleep as soon as I turned off the light.

examples.ruby: 朝[あさ]起[お]きるとすぐにコーヒーを入[い]れることにしている。
examples.english: I make a point of brewing coffee right after I get up in the morning.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]に着[つ]くとすぐに母[はは]から電話[でんわ]がかかってきた。
examples.english: The moment I got to the station, my mother called.

patterns.usage_note: Marks genuine simultaneity rather than succession: the two things hold at the same moment (花火が上がると同時に犬が潜り込んだ). It is the only member of the family that also attaches to a bare noun (卒業と同時に). Outside of time it links two properties as "and at the same time" (難しいと同時に面白い).

examples.ruby: 花火[はなび]が上[あ]がると同時[どうじ]に、犬[いぬ]が机[つくえ]の下[した]に潜[もぐ]り込[こ]んだ。
examples.english: The instant the fireworks went up, the dog burrowed under the desk.

examples.ruby: 電車[でんしゃ]が出発[しゅっぱつ]すると同時[どうじ]にスマホの充電[じゅうでん]が切[き]れた。
examples.english: My phone died at the exact moment the train pulled out.

examples.ruby: 目[め]を閉[と]じると同時[どうじ]に眠[ねむ]りに落[お]ちた。
examples.english: I fell asleep the instant I closed my eyes.

patterns.usage_note: Marks a sudden event breaking out the instant the first one finished (立ち上がった途端、ひどいめまいがした). The た belongs to the pattern (だ途端 after 転んだ and the like), so both clauses are past, and the second is outside the subject's control and often unwelcome. Where や否や presents the second clause as a deliberate act by someone poised for it, た途端 presents it as something nobody saw coming.

examples.ruby: 立[た]ち上[あ]がった途端[とたん]、ひどいめまいがした。
examples.english: The moment I stood up, a wave of dizziness hit me.

examples.ruby: ドアを開[あ]けた途端[とたん]に、猫[ねこ]が外[そと]へ飛[と]び出[だ]した。
examples.english: The instant I opened the door, the cat shot outside.

examples.ruby: 会場[かいじょう]に到着[とうちゃく]した途端[とたん]、雨[あめ]が降[ふ]り出[だ]した。
examples.english: No sooner had I reached the venue than it started to rain.

patterns.usage_note: Marks repetition: each time X is done, Y immediately undoes or repeats it (片付けるそばから子どもが散らかす). It describes a recurring pattern rather than a one-off event, and it almost always carries the speaker's exasperation. Dictionary form frames the habit; た-form frames each individual instance.

examples.ruby: 片付[かたづ]けるそばから子[こ]どもがおもちゃを散[ち]らかす。
examples.english: No sooner do I tidy up than the kids scatter their toys again.

examples.ruby: 教[おし]えたそばから、生徒[せいと]は同[おな]じ漢字[かんじ]を書[か]き間違[まちが]える。
examples.english: No sooner do I teach it than my student misspells the very same kanji again.

examples.ruby: 稼[かせ]ぐそばから使[つか]ってしまうので、貯金[ちょきん]が全[まった]く増[ふ]えない。
examples.english: I spend it as fast as I earn it, so my savings never grow at all.

patterns.usage_note: Marks a second event beginning the instant the first happens, in formal written narration of a single past event (店長が看板を出すや否や). Unlike た途端, the second clause is typically a deliberate action by someone already poised for it. The main clause is a plain past statement: no commands, invitations, intentions or negatives. 否や can be dropped, leaving the stiffer literary や.

examples.ruby: 店長[てんちょう]が看板[かんばん]を出[だ]すや否[いな]や、常連客[じょうれんきゃく]が暖簾[のれん]をくぐった。
examples.english: No sooner had the owner set out the signboard than a regular was ducking under the curtain.

examples.ruby: 犯人[はんにん]は警官[けいかん]の姿[すがた]を見[み]るや否[いな]や逃[に]げ出[だ]した。
examples.english: The culprit took off the instant he spotted the police officer.

examples.ruby: 発表[はっぴょう]が終了[しゅうりょう]するや否[いな]や、質問[しつもん]の手[て]が次々[つぎつぎ]と挙[あ]がった。
examples.english: Hands shot up one after another the moment the presentation ended.

patterns.usage_note: Marks an action taken the instant another one finishes: dictionary-form verb plus なり (帰宅するなり鞄を放り出した), both clauses sharing one subject who is not the speaker, and the second action striking the speaker as abrupt or out of character. The sibling entry pairs representative options for the hearer to choose among (煮るなり焼くなり). It reports past events, so commands, intentions, and negatives cannot follow.

examples.ruby: 新入生[しんにゅうせい]は舞台[ぶたい]に立[た]つなり、台詞[せりふ]を忘[わす]れて笑[わら]い出[だ]した。
examples.english: The moment the new student stepped onstage, he forgot his lines and burst out laughing.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は帰宅[きたく]するなり、鞄[かばん]を放[ほう]り出[だ]して寝[ね]てしまった。
examples.english: The moment my brother got home, he flung down his bag and fell asleep.

examples.ruby: その女性[じょせい]は私[わたし]の顔[かお]を見[み]るなり、大声[おおごえ]で泣[な]き出[だ]した。
examples.english: The woman burst into loud sobs the instant she saw my face.

patterns.usage_note: Attaches to a dictionary-form verb to mark an event following instantly on the one just named: 幕が下りるや means the moment the curtain came down. The sibling lane is the everyday particle や joining nouns as representative examples (鍵や財布). Confined to literary and news narration; the main clause reports a single past fact, so commands, intentions, and negatives do not follow it.

examples.ruby: 老[お]いた漁師[りょうし]は風[かぜ]の向[む]きが変[か]わるや、黙[だま]って舵[かじ]を切[き]った。
examples.english: The instant the wind shifted, the old fisherman silently put the rudder over.

examples.ruby: 男[おとこ]は札束[さつたば]を見[み]るや、目[め]の色[いろ]を変[か]えた。
examples.english: The moment the man laid eyes on the wad of bills, his eyes lit up.

examples.ruby: 幕[まく]が下[お]りるや、客席[きゃくせき]から深[ふか]い溜[た]め息[いき]が漏[も]れた。
examples.english: The moment the curtain came down, a deep sigh escaped the audience.

patterns.usage_note: Marks a second action starting before the first has even finished, as if the subject had been waiting to pounce (チャイムが鳴るが早いか校庭へ駆け出した). It is more dramatic than や否や and belongs to vivid narration of a past scene. The following clause is a plain past statement, never a command, invitation, intention or negative.

examples.ruby: チャイムが鳴[な]るが早[はや]いか、子[こ]どもたちは校庭[こうてい]へ駆[か]け出[だ]した。
examples.english: The instant the chime sounded, the children tore off toward the schoolyard.

examples.ruby: 皿[さら]に唐揚[からあ]げを盛[も]るが早[はや]いか、四方[しほう]から手[て]が伸[の]びてきた。
examples.english: The fried chicken was hardly on the plate before hands came at it from every side.

examples.ruby: そのニュースが流[なが]れるが早[はや]いか、店[みせ]の前[まえ]には長[なが]い列[れつ]ができた。
examples.english: No sooner had the news broken than a long line formed in front of the shop.
